strings.name: Smiljan Radić
strings.summary: Radić built a small Chilean practice around rough stone, translucent shells, houses and temporary structures, pursuing questions of shelter. Buildings may look fragile or unfinished while precise construction creates intense spatial experiences. His Serpentine Pavilion brought international attention, followed by the 2026 Pritzker Architecture Prize. Collaborations and his foundation also foster exchange across disciplines.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Explores materials, landscape and structure through Chilean buildings and the Serpentine Pavilion, developing influence across regions.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Santiago, Chile; raised in a family with Croatian and British roots.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Architecture graduate of Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile in 1989; further history study in Venice and extensive travel.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Light shells and massive stones
strings.highlights.h1.text: The 2014 Serpentine Pavilion set a fiberglass shell on boulders to create an open yet sheltered public space.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Making anew within existing buildings
strings.highlights.h2.text: NAVE retained a damaged historic building and inserted performance spaces, extending urban memory through adaptation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Received the Pritzker in Mexico
strings.timeline.t1.text: Accepted the 2026 architecture prize at Chapultepec Castle and lectured at UNAM the next day.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Biobío theater completed
strings.timeline.t2.text: A translucent envelope and internal structure organized light, acoustics and public cultural activity.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Founded a fragile architecture foundation
strings.timeline.t3.text: Established a Santiago platform supporting experimental architecture through exhibitions, research and exchange.
strings.timeline.t4.title: NAVE arts space completed
strings.timeline.t4.text: Adapted a historic house for rehearsal, workshops and performance, including a rooftop tent.
strings.timeline.t5.title: London Serpentine Pavilion opened
strings.timeline.t5.text: Designed the annual temporary pavilion as both a café and a place for public events.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Restaurant Mestizo completed
strings.timeline.t6.text: Used boulders as structural supports, connecting weight, landscape and everyday gathering.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Established his own office
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began independent practice in Santiago, later collaborating repeatedly with sculptor Marcela Correa.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed architecture education
strings.timeline.t8.text: After graduation, further study in Venice and travel expanded connections among art, history and construction.
